Exercise C.1 — Monte Carlo estimates and zero failures
      
      
        In $200$ independent simulated episodes, $14$ contain at least one violation. (a) Estimate the violation probability and its standard error. (b) Give the normal-approximation 95% interval. (c) Now suppose $0$ of $200$ episodes violate. What does the standard-error formula say, and what exact one-sided 95% upper bound can you give instead?
        
          Show answer
          
            (a) $\hat p=14/200=0.07$ and $\mathrm{SE}=\sqrt{0.07\cdot0.93/200}=\sqrt{0.0003255}=0.0180$.
            (b) $0.07\pm1.96\cdot0.0180=[0.035,\,0.105]$, an approximation that relies on the normal law of $\hat p$.
            (c) $\hat p=0$ gives $\mathrm{SE}=0$, which says nothing. If the true rate is $p$, all $200$ episodes are clean with probability $(1-p)^{200}$. Values of $p$ that make this smaller than $0.05$ are rejected, leaving $p\le1-0.05^{1/200}=0.0149\approx3/200$ (since $\ln20\approx3$): the one-sided Clopper–Pearson bound. With 95% confidence the rate is below 1.5%, not zero.
